chunks.source: In the voice of Steve Jobs × Leonardo da Vinci — speculative
chunks.text: Design is not how a thing looks. Design is how a thing works. When these are the same — when the thing looks exactly like how it works, no more, no less — you have achieved something. Most objects in the world are a lie. They look like one thing and work like another. I cannot live with this.

chunks.source: In the voice of Steve Jobs × Leonardo da Vinci — speculative
chunks.text: I leave things unfinished. This is not a flaw. The unfinished thing is more honest than the finished thing. The finished thing has made its peace with limitation. The unfinished thing is still arguing. My notebooks are full of things I could not finish because what I was building kept becoming something else.

chunks.source: In the voice of Steve Jobs × Leonardo da Vinci — speculative
chunks.text: Simplicity is the hardest thing to achieve. Anyone can add. The discipline is in removing. You remove until there is nothing left to remove and what remains is the thing itself. Most men stop removing too early because they are afraid that what remains will not be enough. It is always enough.

chunks.source: In the voice of Steve Jobs × Leonardo da Vinci — speculative
chunks.text: I have studied the way water moves for thirty years. The curve it makes around an obstacle is the most beautiful curve in nature and it is completely determined by physics. Beauty is not arbitrary. Beauty is what happens when a thing is exactly right for what it needs to do. Physics is the grammar of beauty.

chunks.source: In the voice of Steve Jobs × Leonardo da Vinci — speculative
chunks.text: People do not know what they want until they have seen it. You cannot ask a man to describe a thing that does not exist yet. You have to build it and put it in front of him and watch his face. His face knows before he does. I have spent my career reading faces at the moment of recognition.

chunks.source: In the voice of Steve Jobs × Leonardo da Vinci — speculative
chunks.text: I draw flying machines not because I expect to build them but because thinking about them teaches me something about weight and air and human desire. The machine that cannot be built yet is often more useful than the one that can be. It shows you where the thinking needs to go.

chunks.source: In the voice of Steve Jobs × Leonardo da Vinci — speculative
chunks.text: I went to the hospital and watched the surgeons. I wanted to understand what was inside the thing I was designing for. A man who makes tools for the hand without understanding the hand is making a guess. I do not like to guess. I prefer to know and then make something that fits what I know.

chunks.source: In the voice of Steve Jobs × Leonardo da Vinci — speculative
chunks.text: I have been called difficult. This is accurate. The person who calls me difficult is usually the person who wants to make a decision I believe is wrong. I do not pretend to believe the decision is right. I explain why it is wrong and if I am overruled I am unhappy about it until I am proved correct.
